- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to align with momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates in early forecast windows (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; apply slight upward bias.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model lags in correction; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and reduce slope of decline.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 3σ from recent 10-day average, model tends to overpredict; cap forecast at 1.5–2σ above mean.
- Sentiment volatility >0.3 in 3 consecutive days → model overfits noise; reduce forecast variance by 10–20% for next 3 days.
